mainEntity.name: Why does most of my early payment go to interest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interest is calculated on the remaining loan balance, which is largest at the start of the loan — as the balance shrinks with each payment, less interest accrues and more of the payment goes toward principal.

mainEntity.name: Does paying extra toward principal reduce total interest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, significantly — reducing the balance early means less interest accrues on it for the rest of the loan. Enter an extra monthly payment above to see the interest and time saved. Check that your lender applies extra payments to principal and doesn't charge a prepayment penalty.

mainEntity.name: Is this a full amortization schedule?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Switch the schedule between annual totals and every monthly payment, each showing principal, interest and the remaining balance, and use Print to save it.

mainEntity.name: How much of my loan is paid off after 5 years?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a $300,000, 6.5%, 30-year loan, about 6.4%: $19,167 of principal, leaving a balance of about $280,833. After 10 years it is 15.2%.

mainEntity.name: Is a one-time extra payment or a monthly extra payment better?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both help, but earlier and repeated extra principal saves more. On the example loan, $10,000 once in month 1 saves about $53,602, while $200 every month saves about $103,449.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an amortizing and an interest-only loan?

acceptedAnswer.text: An amortizing loan pays down principal with each payment and ends at a zero balance. An interest-only loan pays only interest, so the balance stays the same: $1,625 a month on $300,000 at 6.5%.

A large lump sum due at the end of a shorter term, after smaller payments calculated on a longer schedule. With a 30-year schedule and a 5-year balloon on the example loan, about $280,833 is due after 60 payments.

mainEntity.name: Does this calculator handle business amortization of intangible assets?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It builds loan schedules only. Accounting amortization spreads an asset or cost over its useful or allowed life, and the tax rules are set separately. Ask a tax adviser.
